title: Projection base change at integral coefficients
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, an integer $n\ge1$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $S$ be a six-functor datum at these coefficients [def-sf-datum], with the specified operation and comparison data [def-fix-six-functor-datum].

Work at $\Lambda=R$ in the bounded constructible derived-complete integral categories $D^b_c(T,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square of finite-type $k$-schemes. Assume $f$ is separated, and supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ with $j$ open, $p$ proper and $pj=f$, together with its Cartesian base change $c'=(j',p')$; all squares and factorizations are part of the specified compactified square. No separatedness of $g$ or of the structure morphisms is assumed. Write $U_u=Lu^*$, $F=Rf_!^c$, $F'=Rf'_!^{c'}$, and $P_f(K,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c$, using the datum's recorded projection components [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates, def-exchange-projection]. Let $e_M:U_gFM\to F'U_{g'}M$ be the specified compact-support exchange, with only the datum's endpoint identifications. Let $\mu_u(A,B):U_u(A\otimes B)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_uA\otimes U_uB$ be the canonical normalized tensor-pullback comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], and let $\kappa_L:U_{g'}U_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{f'}U_gL$ be the inverse pullback compositor to $U_{fg'}L$, transport through $fg'=gf'$, then the pullback compositor to $U_{f'}U_gL$. Tensor and pullback at $R$ are completed, at $E$ rationalized, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ represented over a common finite field. For the inputs specified below, the following equality holds:
$$\begin{aligned}
F'\bigl((1\otimes\kappa_L)\circ\mu_{g'}(K,U_fL)\bigr)\circ e_{K\otimes U_fL}\circ U_g(P_f(K,L))
={}&P_{f'}(U_{g'}K,U_gL)\circ(e_K\otimes1)\circ\mu_g(FK,L).
\end{aligned}$$
Both sides have source $U_g(FK\otimes L)$ and target $F'(U_{g'}K\otimes U_{f'}U_gL)$, using exactly the specified maps, rather than independently chosen isomorphisms.

Here $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,R)$, and $L$ satisfies the specified uniform finite-reduction Tor-amplitude predicate: there exist integers $a\le b$ such that every finite reduction of $L$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

At integral coefficients prove an equality of completed arrows before evaluation, not by assuming finite evaluations are faithful. The open-factor equation gives the completed domains and monoidality; transpose the proper-factor routes using the counit/mate identity, then paste. Verbatim retained old parent argument, in source order:
By [def-sf-pf, def-exchange-projection], use $\operatorname{PF}^c=Rp_*(\gamma_j)\pi_p$. The underlying operation datum of [def-sf-datum], on its domains $K\in D^b_c$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}$, satisfies the stage laws [lem-sf-projection-finite-stage-laws, lem-sf-projection-integral-stage-laws, lem-sf-projection-field-stage-laws] (mate calculus of the counit projection and the open tensor map at each coefficient stage, without invertibility of the projection maps), which give naturality in $K,L$, the $\alpha_{g,f}$ pentagon, compactification compatibility and the proper identification. For the identity clause, use the four proved stage lemmas of [lem-sf-projection-identity-assembly] on the underlying operation datum. They construct the normalized units by full-faithful cancellation of the compositor, prove uniqueness by naturality and cancellation, and transport the proper counit identity to every compactification by the stage proper-coincidence laws. Their finite full-faithfulness calculation is proved directly from the derived intrinsic identity pullback; the remaining fullness and the proper counit calculations are the two smaller source obligations recorded below that node. Use proved private equations for the existing support and finite-Tor identity comparisons to match the statement here without repeated large coefficient-category unfolding. This retains the identity-adjunction and proper-coincidence route of the unit.

Choose $f=pj$ and its Cartesian base change; by [def-exchange-projection] $\operatorname{PF}^c=R(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=R'(\beta)e$. Apply [lem-sf-pf-open-base-change-square] with $M=j_!K$, $Q=M\otimes FL$: it supplies all completed constructible domains, monoidality of $\theta:F'G\cong HF$, and the open-factor equality. The ordinary adjunctions are [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). The proper exchange $e$ is their specified mate of $\theta$ by [def-exchange-projection, fix-lem-exchanges], and $\pi_p$ is the counit projection. Apply [lem-sp-categorical-projection-mate-square] with its adjunctions $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$, $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$, $N_D=G$, $N_C=H$, $\alpha=\theta$, $\varphi=\mu_F$, $\varphi'=\mu_{F'}$, $m_C=\mu_H$, $m_D=\mu_G$; its hypothesis ComparisonCompatible is the monoidality equation just cited. Its conclusion is $R'(d)e_QG(\pi_{p;M,L})=\pi_{p';HM,GL}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L}$ with $d=(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})\mu_H$, the proper-factor hypothesis of [lem-sf-pf-compactification-pasting]; the open one is the equality above. That pasting identity gives the displayed square: its target comparison is $La^*JFL\cong J'HFL\to J'F'GL\cong Lf'^*GL$. Refinement compatibility and square naturality in [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(4), with projection compatibility from step 1, remove the compactification choice; the naturality clause of the pasting lemma gives naturality in the morphism data. At finite coefficients apply [lem-sf-finite-base-change-transport]: its proof identifies each constructible-coordinate route under faithful realization, substitutes the existing fixed-scalar diamond equality, cancels the common target isomorphism, and reflects equality through the full inclusion. This retains the proper/open mate calculation and adds no separatedness of the horizontal map.

Exact sorried source theorem header:
theorem sixFunctorProjection_baseChange_integral (S : SixFunctorDatum D C E n hn) :
    ∀ (Q : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
      [IsSeparated Q.f.hom.left]
      (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E Q.X.obj.left)
      (L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E Q.Y.obj.left),
      S.toSixFunctorOperationDatum.integralFiniteTorDomain Q.Y L →
      (S.higher.integral.pull Q.g).map ((S.higher.integralExchange Q).projectionComponent K L) ≫
        sixFunctorProjectionExchange (S.higher.integralExchange Q)
          (((S.higher.integralTensor Q.X).obj K).obj ((S.higher.integral.pull Q.f).obj L)) ≫
        (S.higher.integral.support Q.f' Q.compactification').map
          ((sixFunctorProjectionIntegralMu S Q.g' K
            ((S.higher.integral.pull Q.f).obj L)).hom ≫
            ((S.higher.integralTensor Q.X').obj ((S.higher.integral.pull Q.g').obj K)).map
              (((S.higher.integral.pullComposition Q.g' Q.f).inv.app L) ≫
                eqToHom (congrArg
                  (fun f ↦ (S.higher.integral.pull f).obj L) Q.squareComm) ≫
                (S.higher.integral.pullComposition Q.f' Q.g).hom.app L)) =
      (sixFunctorProjectionIntegralMu S Q.g
        ((S.higher.integral.support Q.f Q.compactification).obj K) L).hom ≫
        ((S.higher.integralTensor Q.Y').map
          (sixFunctorProjectionExchange (S.higher.integralExchange Q) K)).app
            ((S.higher.integral.pull Q.g).obj L) ≫
        (S.higher.integralExchange (compactSupportProjectionSquare Q.f'
          Q.compactification')).projectionComponent
          ((S.higher.integral.pull Q.g').obj K) ((S.higher.integral.pull Q.g).obj L)
